newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea says union arrests must go ahead.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says union arrests must go ahead.

text.p: South Korean cabinet ministers on Wednesday decided to proceed with the arrest of union leaders spearheading wildcat strikes, a statement by the Prime Minister's Office said.
Arrests of leaders of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions sheltering at Seoul's Myongdong Cathedral "cannot be delayed", it said.
The decision was taken in a meeting of economic ministers and security-related ministers, which was chaired by Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung, Lee's spokesman told Reuters.
"The ministers agreed that the illegal activity by some union leaders could no longer be left unchecked," he said.
"The meeting confirmed the government's position that the arrest of the leaders of illegal strikes cannot be delayed even with some negative effects and repercussions," the statement added.
The confederation had called for indefinite "all-out" strikes from Wednesday in protest at a controversial labour law, but most public services across the country were operating normally.
